chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no valid charity (sadaqah) nor manumission (itq) except that which is done with the intention of seeking the Face of Allah, Exalted and Glorious."

key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (metonymy for seeking His pleasure)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for charity and manumission to be valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Reported in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith clarifies that the validity of charity (sadaqah) and manumission (itq) is contingent upon pure intention (ikhlas) for Allah’s sake, excluding worldly motives. This aligns with the Shia scholarly emphasis on the inner dimension of worship, where the spiritual acceptance of the act depends on the sincerity of the heart rather than merely the external performance.
